question: At a hypothetical 20% advertising assignment capacity, does estimated uplift improve released-benchmark visit contrast over random targeting and response ranking?
technique: T-learner uplift ranking with held-out inverse-propensity policy evaluation
sample: SplitMix64(source row ordinal) modulo 20 equals zero; all source rows scanned
split: Identical f0:f11 profiles hashed together; hash modulo 100: train <50, validation 50:69, test >=70

excluded.treatment: assignment, never a baseline ranking feature

selection: Highest validation IPW incremental visits per eligible user at top 20%; no test refit or selection
primary: Paired test uplift-policy minus 20% random allocation IPW contrast; also compare response ranking
propensity: Training assignment share only; sensitivity to 0.85 and training-only logistic assignment model
uncertainty: 500 Poisson(1) identical-profile cluster multiplier replicates, percentile 95%, conditional on fixed fits, ranking and assignment estimate; pointwise, not simultaneous
sensitivity: DR score with fixed independent training-only outcome models
estimand_limit: Privacy-altered released advertising benchmark contrast, not original experiment ITT, individual causal truth, retention uplift or employer impact
